items.title: Hunger that runs ahead of the body
items.author: Moyu Lyu, Kevin W. Williams
items.content: <article>In this issue of Neuron, Walker, Lowenstein et al. identify PVHSim2 neurons as excitatory input that rapidly activates ARCAgRP hunger neurons. By tracking predicted food availability, these cells help the brain anticipate an energy deficit before the body registers one.</article>

items.title: Sculpting functional brain drainage
items.author: Angelina Persaud, Max A. Tischfield
items.content: <article>Mechanisms directing meningeal lymphatic development have remained largely unexplored. Tavares et al. identify macrophage-mediated sculpting as a developmental program that establishes cerebrospinal fluid drainage pathways, revealing how disrupted lymphatic maturation may contribute to neurodevelopmental disorders.</article>

items.title: Aggregation and propagation of TAF15 trigger neurodegeneration
items.author: Lanxia Meng, Congcong Liu, Huangchuan Gong, Yan Gao, Meihui Li, Han Liu, Hanying Teng, Min Xiong, Hui Liu, Mingmin Yan, Dae Ki Hong, Seong Su Kang, Jing Xiong, Zhentao Zhang
items.content: <article>Meng et al. report that TAF15 forms amyloid fibrils capable of propagation both in vitro and in vivo. The spread of TAF15 pathology triggers progressive neurodegeneration, cognitive impairment, and anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. These findings establish TAF15 aggregation as a key pathogenic driver of neurodegenerative disease.</article>
